OUR REPLICATION STUDY
Our replication and extension of Fernbach etal.(2013) involved two main changes to the original

study. First, we examined different policy areas in a different political context. Fernbach etal.(2013)

conducted their study in the United States examining six types of policies, as did Crawford and

decisions.reason: Walker et al. (2023) re-tests the three experiments of Fernbach et al. (2013) (Study 1 replicates Fernbach et al.'s Experiment 2, Study 2 replicates Experiment 3, and Study 3 replicates Experiment 1), which is already represented in shipped row 2400 (paired with blind target 0). Crawford and Ruscio (2021) is an earlier replication of Fernbach et al. (2013)—published after Walker et al.'s 2020 studies were conducted—that is cited only for literature context, power comparison, and discussion. Per the codebook, an earlier replication attempt that this paper does not itself re-test is not a target, and no other untested original exists to replace this row.

decisions.quote:
To contribute to this debate, we replicated and extended
Fernbach etal.'s(2013) three experiments to include new designs, greater statistical power, and

a new context to test if procedural policy knowledge can shatter citizens' knowledge illusion.

In Study 1, mechanistic explanation and enumerating reasons interventions strengthened ex-

treme positions. In Study 2, mechanistic explanation increased the relationship between posi-

tion extremity and political donation. In Study 3, mechanistic explanations moderated policy
understanding but did not significantly change extreme positions. We found that mechanistic

explanation and reason enumeration can elicit extreme positions or have null effects, withhold-

ing support towards Fernbach etal.'s(2013) original study but partially supporting Crawford

and Ruscio's(2021) replication.
decisions.reason: Outcomes are original-specific. Because Crawford and Ruscio (2021) in row 1254 is a contextual earlier replication rather than a tested original (and row 1254 is removed via original corrected_value={"action":"remove_row"}), no valid replication outcome exists for this row. Shipped erroneously copied the failed outcome quote directed at Fernbach et al. (2013) (covered by row 2400) onto Crawford and Ruscio (2021), whose null findings the authors actually say their results partially support.

decisions.quote:
We conducted three high-value

replications and extensions to examine the applicability
of Fernbach's proposed theory among a sample of 5,139

citizens in postconflict Hong Kong.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree that the FLoRA record is a replication study collecting new experimental data (N = 5,139 across Studies 1–3 in Hong Kong) to re-test Fernbach et al. (2013); the non-target status of Crawford and Ruscio (2021) on row 1254 is resolved by removing the row via the original field.
